transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you—what brings you in today?

Hi… yeah, so I guess the main thing is I keep getting pulled off track really easily. Like I’ll be working on a dashboard I’m supposed to finish, and then one Slack ping comes in, or even just a song lyric gets stuck in my head, or I suddenly think of another project idea, and then I’ve totally lost what I was doing.

It’s frustrating because it sounds small, but it happens enough that I feel like I’m constantly trying to find the thread again.
Thinking back to when you were a kid, say before middle school, do you remember having similar trouble staying focused or getting easily distracted, or is this more of a recent thing as an adult?

Yeah, I think it was there pretty early. Like in elementary school my teachers would write those report card comments—not terrible grades or anything, but stuff like I rushed through worksheets, or I’d lose track of the directions halfway through.

And during group work I guess I’d talk over other kids, which is kind of embarrassing to think about now. My parents also used to sit next to me when I did homework, because if they didn’t I’d just… drift off, or get up and start doing something else before I’d actually finished. So, no, I don’t think it’s only an adult thing.

These focus and distraction issues you’re describing—do they cause you clear problems in more than one area of your life, for example both at work and also in things like home responsibilities, hobbies, or relationships?

Yeah, definitely more than one area. Work-wise—well, freelance work, since I’m not in like a normal job right now—I’ve actually lost a couple small contracts because I didn’t follow through cleanly. Like I had good ideas at the start, and then the delivery got messy or late enough that they just didn’t come back.

And there was this portfolio competition I really wanted to enter—sorry, random, but I had this whole concept for it that I was excited about—and I missed out because I couldn’t get everything together reliably. It also kind of affects friends or people I collaborate with. They’ll say they like my ideas, but I can tell some of them are hesitant to actually work with me because they’re not sure I’ll be dependable. That part feels pretty awful, honestly.
Outside of the distraction and follow-through issues, do you find yourself worrying a lot about different things in your life, in a way that feels hard to control or switch off?

Um… I don’t know. I mean, I worry about things sometimes, like everyone does, I guess, especially if I’ve missed something or I’m not sure what someone thinks of me. But I wouldn’t say I’m sitting there worrying about everything all day.

Though now that you ask, I’m trying to think—because sometimes I get stuck in my head, but it’s more like replaying a thing or thinking about what I need to do, and then I’ll suddenly remember I forgot to text someone back. Sorry, that’s not really what you asked. I guess I’m not totally sure what counts as “hard to switch off.”

In the past few months, have you had periods lasting at least a couple of weeks where you felt on edge or keyed up most days, like your body and mind just wouldn’t settle even when nothing specific was happening right then?

Yeah… kind of. I don’t know if I’d describe it as, like, constant anxiety or something, but I do get this really uncomfortable restless feeling.

Like if I’m stuck on a long Zoom call, or I’m supposed to sit quietly and work in one place, after a while it feels like there’s pressure building up in my body and I need to get up or pace around. Or at least be doing something with my hands. I’ll try to look normal, but inside I’m sort of like, please let me move.

Sorry, that probably sounds dramatic—it’s not like every second of the day, but it has been happening lately when I have to stay still for too long.

When you get that restless, keyed‑up feeling, is it usually because you’re actively worrying about something bad that might happen, or does it also show up when you’re not particularly worried and are just bored or stuck doing something uninteresting?

It’s not always because I’m worrying something bad will happen. Sometimes it’s literally just because I’m stuck sitting there, like on a long Zoom call or trying to work quietly in one place.

I’ll start feeling this kind of pressure in my body, like I need to get up or pace, or at least do something with my hands. It’s more like being trapped in stillness, if that makes sense. I mean, sometimes I might also be thinking about what I’m supposed to be doing, but the restless feeling can show up even when I’m just bored or the thing is really uninteresting.

When you’re doing something you actually find really interesting or fun, like a favorite hobby or a project you’re excited about, do you still find your mind drifting off or your body feeling restless, or does that mostly happen only with boring or routine tasks?

Um, I think it’s mostly with boring or routine things… or like when I’m expected to just sit there and not move. If I’m on a long Zoom call, or I have to quietly work in one place, I start getting this uncomfortable pressure in my body, like I need to get up or pace around, or at least do something with my hands.

If it’s something fun, I can get more absorbed, I guess—though sorry, now I’m thinking of this craft project I did where I sat there for way too long and didn’t notice the time. But yeah, the restless feeling is way more obvious when I’m stuck doing something dull or having to sit still.
Over the past month, have you often felt down, depressed, or like you’ve lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

Um… I don’t think so? Not in a clear way. Like, I have days where I’m kind of blah or I don’t feel like doing stuff, but I don’t know if I’d call it depressed.

And the interest thing is hard because sometimes I’ll be really into something and then suddenly not want to touch it for a while—like I had this whole phase where I was reorganizing my room and watching videos about shelves, which sounds ridiculous, but then I just stopped. But that feels more like I moved on or got bored, not like I couldn’t enjoy anything.

So… I guess I haven’t really noticed feeling down most days or losing pleasure in everything, no.
Lately, have you been having trouble either falling asleep at night or staying asleep through the night often enough that it feels like a real problem for you?

I’m not totally sure how to answer that. I mean, my sleep can be kind of inconsistent, but I haven’t really been tracking it or anything.

Sometimes I stay up too late because I get caught doing something, like scrolling or reorganizing something random, and then suddenly it’s way later than I thought. But I don’t know if that counts as trouble falling asleep exactly, or just me not going to bed when I should.

Staying asleep… I don’t think I’ve noticed that being a big thing? Like, not enough that I’d call it a major problem lately, I guess.

When you’re doing something you genuinely find interesting or fun, like a hobby or a project you’re really into, do you still often lose track of what you’re doing because your attention jumps to other thoughts or distractions?

Yeah, that does happen, even when I’m into the thing. I think that’s kind of the main reason I came in, honestly—I get pulled off track so easily.

Like I’ll be working on a dashboard or something I actually care about finishing, and then one Slack ping happens, or I hear a song lyric and it reminds me of something, or I get this random idea for a totally different project, and suddenly I’m not on the dashboard anymore. I’ll be three tabs away looking something up and then I’m like, wait, what was I doing?

It’s annoying because it’s not just with boring stuff. Fun things hold me better, but they don’t make me immune to getting yanked in another direction.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a lifelong pattern, beginning in elementary school, of marked distractibility, difficulty sustaining attention, and poor follow‑through that now causes clear functional impairment in work and collaborative relationships. Symptoms are present across settings (school history, current freelance work, social/creative collaborations), are not limited to periods of low mood or high anxiety, and include both cognitive inattention (easily pulled off task, losing the thread, drifting off during homework) and situational restlessness when required to sit still for boring tasks. There is no evidence of a pervasive anxiety syndrome, depressive episode, primary insomnia, or isolated stress reaction severe enough to account for the full picture. This is most consistent with ADHD, predominantly inattentive type (F90.0).
